title: test(network-escape): serve the last probe from a double and retire the burn-down list (objectui#7307)
body:
Fixes #7307

Batch 6 — the **last** row of the network-escape burn-down. The ledger reaches zero here, so the burn-down machinery is retired with it.

## BEFORE (base `fc32921aa`)

`pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowNodeInspector.specKeys.test.tsx` — exit **0** (green *while* escaping, which is objectui#6640 exactly). Three attributed escapes, one per render:

```
[network-escape - known - objectui#6640] packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowNodeInspector.specKeys.test.tsx -> http://localhost:3000/api/v1/meta/object
  The ECONNREFUSED stack near this line belongs to that file. Serve the
  probe from a double, then delete its line from KNOWN_ESCAPES in
  vitest.setup.network-escape-guard.ts.
```

plus 3 × `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000`.

`pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/network-escape-ledger.test.ts` on the base — exit **0**, 3 tests, `PINNED_LEDGER.length === 1`.

**Traced call path:** `FlowNodeInspector` renders `FlowReferenceField` for every reference-kind key on the selected node; `useMetadataListOptions` (`FlowReferenceField.tsx:638`) resolves options through `MetadataClient.list(type)` — `GET /api/v1/meta/object` over the authenticated wrapper's bare global `fetch` (`packages/auth/src/createAuthenticatedFetch.ts`). Under happy-dom that global is a real HTTP client and the document URL defaults to `http://localhost:3000`, so the relative path resolved to a live socket. Same path the batch-5 sibling `FlowNodeInspector.inactiveRetained.test.tsx` fixed.

## AFTER (`e09bb3e50`)

| run | exit | result | escapes | ECONNREFUSED |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| target file alone | 0 | 5 passed | **0** | **0** |
| `inspectors/` + `scripts/__tests__/` union, at final HEAD | 0 | 183 files, 4194 passed / 1 skipped | **0** | **0** |
| `record-details.hideEmptyRetired-7129.test.tsx` | 0 | 3 passed | 0 | 0 |

The guard's `afterEach` is silent for the whole `inspectors/` directory: 67 files, 770 tests, not one socket.

The double is the shape the sibling carries — a **recording router**, not a blanket stub. It answers `/api/v1/meta/object` with an empty `{ type, items: [] }` registry (byte-identical to what the failed read already produced through the hook's `.catch`, so no assertion moves), records every URL, and its `afterEach` fails on any URL outside that route. Teardown order per objectui#7439: `cleanup()` **before** `vi.unstubAllGlobals()`.

## The retirement — decision (b), and why

The old pin's own non-vacuity floor prescribed this, verbatim: *"If the ledger genuinely reached zero … delete the guard's KNOWN_ESCAPES machinery and this pin together, rather than leaving a pin that asserts nothing."*

**GONE** from `vitest.setup.network-escape-guard.ts`: the `KNOWN_ESCAPES` set; the attributed-stderr branch that kept listed files green (with the now-dead `writeStderr` / `StderrHost` it existed for); the `unknown = seen.filter(!KNOWN_ESCAPES.has)` split; the `Do NOT add this file to KNOWN_ESCAPES` line of the `Fix:` text; and the header's burn-down section, rewritten to record that the list reached zero on this card.

**KEPT, untouched**: the recording `fetch` wrapper and the `afterEach` that fails ANY escape in ANY file — the standing guard of objectui#6640, which was never part of the burn-down. Its `Fix:` remedy (double + teardown order) stays, because it is still the remedy.

**The pin: (b), replaced, not deleted** — `scripts/__tests__/network-escape-ledger.test.ts` now pins that the machinery is gone and the standing guard is still installed. Four axes:

- **实际业务需求** — measured, not speculative. The pressure the old pin resisted (its own docstring: "an author who hit the guard's red could make it green by adding a line") did not end with the list, it went **up**: every escape is now red on its first run with **no list to join**, so the cheapest wrong fix available to the next author is to *re-create* the list — one line, green on arrival. Option (a) leaves nothing resisting that.
- **项目长远合理性** — contract-first. The standing guard is the contract "no test reaches a socket"; (b) pins that it has no escape hatch. This repo's own precedent argues for it directly: the guard's docstring said the list "may only shrink" and that was **not true until a pin made it true**. Same reasoning, one step later.
- **防 AI 写代码犯错** — decisive. A re-added list is exactly 宽容-as-cover: an AI makes a red green by *declaring an exception* instead of fixing the escape, and the tolerated path applies repo-wide and silently. (b) makes re-introduction structurally loud; (a) makes it routine.
- **创业阶段不扩散需求** — both options retire *immediately*; (b) is no staged window, it asserts ABSENCE. It is not capability expansion: zero product surface, zero published bytes, ~130 lines of test replacing a file that already existed in a directory of 116 such pins, and the file **count stays flat**. The mild line-count pull toward (a) is outweighed by axis 3, which this repo ranks higher.

Kept at the same path deliberately: an agent who greps `network-escape-ledger` — because the guard's old text told them the two move together — lands on the retirement pin and reads why there is no list.

The absence checks read the guard through `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, the tree's one answer to "comment, or code?". That is load-bearing: the guard's header now *explains* at length that there is no `KNOWN_ESCAPES`, so a naive text search finds the name in prose and the pin could never go green. A `PROSE_ONLY` control asserts masking is actually working, so the negatives cannot pass over unmasked text.

## Ablation — the retirement pin reds if the list comes back

Mutated the **committed** tree (`git checkout HEAD --` restore, absolute paths, `trap … EXIT INT TERM`): re-added an `export const KNOWN_ESCAPES = new Set([...])` to the guard.

On-disk proof, not an editor exit code — `export const KNOWN_ESCAPES` count `0 → 1`; blob `94c4d099…` → `19226b8c…`.

Result: exit **1**, `2 failed | 3 passed` — the namespace test (`exports nothing`) and the code test (`declares no allowlist`), which is the predicted direction and both halves.

Restore proven by bytes, not by an exit code: `git hash-object` back to `94c4d099bb946c65de342ebc0482e106ed17bbaa` = the HEAD blob; `git diff HEAD` empty; `git status` clean.

## Standing-guard proof (scratch, never committed)

A scratch test in a file no list ever named, fetching `http://localhost:3000/api/v1/x`, under the guard:

```
Error: Network escape: this test reached a REAL socket at http://localhost:3000/api/v1/x.
  file: scripts/__tests__/zz-standing-guard-scratch.test.ts
  test: scratch: an escape in a file no list ever named > reaches a real socket …
```

Exit **1**, with the full `Fix:` text and no trailing "Do NOT add this file to KNOWN_ESCAPES" line. Scratch deleted; `git status` clean and `git diff HEAD` empty afterwards.

## Mentions updated

- `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-details.hideEmptyRetired-7129.test.tsx` — its "⛔ Not `KNOWN_ESCAPES`: that list only shrinks" comment now says there is no list to join at all.
- `scripts/check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` — its `KNOWN_HAND_SPELLINGS` header cited the ledger as "the same shape"; now cites it in the past tense and points at what the file pins today.

**Deliberately not touched:** `.changeset/network-escape-batch{1,2,3,4}.md` and `.changeset/network-escapes-batch5.md` name `KNOWN_ESCAPES` / `PINNED_LEDGER`. They are pending release notes describing what *those* PRs did, and they are accurate as written; rewriting four other PRs' unreleased changesets is the third-party touch `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` exists to discourage. `AGENTS.md` does not name the list.

## Gates (exit codes, at `e09bb3e50`)

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `vitest run …/FlowNodeInspector.specKeys.test.tsx` | 0 (5 passed) |
| `vitest run …/inspectors/ scripts/__tests__/` | 0 (183 files, 4194 passed) |
| `vitest run …/record-details.hideEmptyRetired-7129.test.tsx` | 0 (3 passed) |
| `pnpm lint:root` | 0 (0 errors, 32 warnings — all pre-existing) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run type-check` | 0 (both `tsc --noEmit` **and** `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the test files are covered) |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 (6594 files scanned) |
| `pnpm check:entry-guard` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 — 1 changeset, empty frontmatter |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` | 0 — no pre-existing changeset touched |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (all 6 paths) | 0 — NOT GOVERNED |

Dependency closure built first (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build`) — without it `type-check` fails with 16 phantom `TS2307`s from stale/absent `dist/*.d.ts`, which would have read as "your change broke the imports".

Changeset: `.changeset/network-escapes-batch6.md`, empty frontmatter — test-only, no product source touched, nothing to release.
